summary: Series.append exists in pandas 1.5.3 but is deprecated; its default ignore_index=False retains original index labels, and pandas.concat is the recommended replacement.
DataFrame.iteritems exists in pandas 1.5.3, iterates over column name and Series pairs, and is deprecated in favor of DataFrame.items.
Pandas 2.0 removed Series.append and DataFrame.append; use pandas.concat instead.
pandas.concat combines Series or DataFrames. Its default ignore_index=False retains existing index labels; ignore_index=True discards them.
Pandas 2.0 removed Series.iteritems and DataFrame.iteritems; use obj.items instead.
Pandas 2.0.3 supports taking the mean of a selected numeric column after grouping a DataFrame; the shown groupby selected-column mean expression needs no API rename.
Pandas 2.0 removed Int64Index, UInt64Index, and Float64Index. Construct pd.Index with an explicit numeric dtype instead; index values and dtype can be preserved.
Use DatetimeIndex.isocalendar().week to obtain ISO week numbers. For a datetime Series, use Series.dt.isocalendar().week. Check the desired result dtype separately.
Index.is_monotonic was removed in pandas 2.0; use Index.is_monotonic_increasing for the same increasing-order predicate.
DataFrame.to_csv and Series.to_csv removed the line_terminator argument; use lineterminator instead to specify CSV line endings.
DataFrame.set_axis and Series.set_axis removed inplace. Assign the returned object, for example df = df.set_axis(labels, axis=1, copy=False).
read_csv removed error_bad_lines and warn_bad_lines. Use on_bad_lines='warn' to skip malformed lines with a warning, or 'skip' to skip silently.
read_csv removed squeeze. Read the file as a DataFrame and use the returned DataFrame's squeeze('columns') method when a one-column result should be a Series.
